articles.title: Bihar Student Protest: Students Clash With Police During CM Residence March
articles.description: Bihar’s student protest has intensified as thousands of candidates marched in Patna demanding reforms and action over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations. Students are demanding cancellation of disputed exams, including the Bihar Police Sub-Inspector exam, and reforms in BSSC and TRE-4 recruitment. They also want the BPSC Examination Controller, Rajesh Kumar, to be dismissed and arrested over his controversial “dog barking” remark. Although he was suspended and later expressed regret, protesters say suspension is not enough. Students demanded direct talks with Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, refusing to meet district officials. Police stopped the march near Dak Bungalow Chowk using barricades, while protesters broke some barricades and climbed onto police and water-cannon vehicles. Water cannon and lathi-charge allegations further escalated tensions. Students also criticised BPSC’s decision to conduct examinations in two stages instead of a single examination. Meanwhile, farmers protesting against alleged forced land acquisition for a satellite township joined the student movement, demanding fair compensation and opposing the acquisition of their agricultural land.

articles.title: Nitin Gadkari Statement: “New Generation Should Get Responsibility,” Says Union Minister
articles.description: Union Minister Nitin Gadkari’s recent remarks have sparked speculation about his political future. Speaking at an event in Nagpur, Gadkari said that after around 30 years in public life, he cannot work as much as he used to and that it is time to give the new generation an opportunity to take responsibility. Gadkari also emphasized the importance of health, saying that wealth, power and position have little value if one’s health is poor. He described how his lifestyle changed after the COVID period, including adopting a more disciplined routine and regular yoga. His comments have triggered fresh retirement and Cabinet reshuffle speculation, particularly because Gadkari is frequently mentioned in discussions about a possible reshuffle. However, it is important to note that Gadkari has not announced his retirement or said that he is stepping down.

articles.title: 15% decline in Indians seeking admission to UG courses in US: Report
articles.description: Amid the tightening of immigration policies, the number of Indian students seeking admission to US colleges declined by 15 per cent in 2025-26 over the previous year, according to a report. A report, representing over 1,100 institutions, released by the Common App, shows that although application volume for undergraduate admission in the upcoming 2026-27 academic year rose overall, the number of international applicants through March 1 fell 10 per cent, the steepest decline on record. The report by a non-profit organisation recorded a 15 per cent decrease in applicants from India -- the top source for international students in the US. India is the largest source of international students in the US, with over 3.63 lakh enrolling for different courses in the 2024-25 academic year. According to the report, international students contributed USD 41.77 billion to the local economy in the Fall 2025-26. The same number is projected to be 38.37 billion in 2026-27. articles.description: Russia's alleged shadow war in Europe may be moving closer to the heart of Ukraine's military supply chain. Western intelligence assessments reportedly point to a covert network using local operatives to target facilities linked to Ukraine's war effort, with arson and sabotage among the suspected tactics. Recent fires and explosions across several European countries are now drawing scrutiny, raising fresh questions over whether Moscow is testing a new way to hit Ukraine without triggering a direct NATO confrontation. However, Russian involvement has not been proven in every incident, and Moscow has repeatedly rejected such accusations. If the allegations are confirmed, Europe could be facing a quieter but increasingly dangerous front in the Russia-Ukraine war.

articles.title: US launches ‘operation economic outcast’: Trump pressures world leaders to stop dealing with Iran?
articles.description: Donald Trump has launched what his administration calls an “economic D-Day” against Iran. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent unveiled Operation Economic Outcast, vowing to sever Tehran's financial lifelines worldwide and impose a “zero-leakage” sanctions campaign. Washington is targeting digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping while warning foreign governments and businesses against helping Iran. Bessent said Trump is personally calling world leaders and threatened to remove Iran-linked entities from the US dollar system. With dozens of targets already sanctioned, will Trump's financial offensive isolate Tehran or trigger another escalation?

articles.title: Putin turns Kim’s troops into new drone force for Ukraine? 400 N. Korean UAV operators reach Russia
articles.description: North Korea has reportedly deployed about 400 drone operators to Russia as part of an estimated 8,500-strong military contingent, deepening Pyongyang’s role in Moscow’s war effort. Ukrainian military intelligence says most of the force is in Russia’s Kursk region and includes roughly 1,000 engineers and deminers; the drone teams could conduct reconnaissance and strike missions against Ukraine from Russian territory. The claims have not been independently verified, but the deployment could give North Korean personnel crucial experience in modern drone warfare. It follows reports that Pyongyang was considering sending up to 25,000 workers to Russia’s Alabuga drone-production hub in exchange for drone-operations training.
